chunks: From him, from Al-Hajjal, from Thal'aba, from Ali ibn Uqba, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
My father (peace be upon him), whenever a matter grieved him, would gather the women and the children, then supplicate, and they would say 'Ameen'.
ai.seo_question: What did the Imams do when they were grieved or distressed?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this narration highlights Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) strategic use of familial piety, specifically gathering women and children, to invoke divine mercy during times of distress. This practice underscores the Shia scholarly view that the sincere du'a of the 'Aqil (the one who supplicates) is amplified by the collective affirmation of the household, reflecting the broader Islamic principle that communal worship strengthens spiritual resilience.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Al Hajjal, from Sa’alba, from Ali Bin Uqba, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘It was so that whenever a matter grieved myasws fatherasws, heasws would gather the womenfolk and the children, then supplicate, and they would be saying Ameen’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from al-Hajjal from Tha’labah from Ali ibn ‘Uqbah from a man from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
Whenever something saddened my father he would call the ladies and children together. He would then pray and they would say, ‘Amin.’”
